problem: VLN-CE agents on RxR-Habitat suffer from low-level action grounding, weak progress tracking on long fine-grained trajectories, and collapse in the no-sliding setting because they are unaware of collisions and get stuck or stop early.
motivation: RxR-Habitat is a harder, more realistic VLN-CE benchmark: long multilingual trajectories, low-level actions, and sliding forbidden. Prior controllers lose much performance when moved from sliding-allowed to sliding-forbidden environments, so a hierarchical design that reuses discrete-VLN advances and handles collisions is needed.
key_idea: A modular plan-and-control agent: a depth-only candidate waypoint predictor, a HAMT-based history-enhanced planner that picks a waypoint as subgoal, and a non-parametric 'tryout' controller that detects deadlocks and escapes by trial and error.
insight: Decoupling planning from control lets discrete-VLN advances (HAMT history encoder, synthetic-data pretraining) transfer to VLN-CE. The tryout controller recovers most of the no-sliding loss: SR rises from 20.93 to 48.6 without sliding at inference, against 51.98 with sliding allowed. Training with sliding and testing without it beats training without sliding (SR 48.6 vs 45.0). Pretraining on marky-mT5 data, style-transfer augmentation and snapshot ensembling each add small gains (about 0.3-1.3 points).
method: Candidate Waypoints Predictor: predicts a local navigation graph of candidate waypoints from depth only, following Hong et al. 2022. The agent rotates in place to get multiple views, and the rotation steps count toward the action budget.

History Enhanced Planner: HAMT with an extra depth encoding in the vision encoder. A history encoder tracks navigation progress and a multilingual instruction encoder is shared across en/hi/te. It selects one waypoint as the subgoal.

Tryout Controller: converts the subgoal (distance, heading) into low-level actions and detects deadlock by comparing consecutive frames. On deadlock it tries several predefined directions with a single forward action; all tried actions count toward the step budget.

Training: stage 1 is offline pretraining with HAMT proxy tasks (MLM, ITM, SAP/SAR, SPREL) on RxR plus about 1M marky-mT5 synthetic pairs. Stage 2 is online fine-tuning in Habitat with schedule sampling, with sliding allowed in training and forbidden at evaluation.
Extras: style-transfer environment augmentation on RGB during online tuning (EnvEdit) and a snapshot ensemble of two checkpoints at inference.

setting.backbone: HAMT-based planner (RoBERTa multilingual text encoder, CLIP ViT RGB encoder, DDPPO ResNet50 depth encoder) + depth-based waypoint predictor + heuristic tryout controller
setting.training_data: RxR-Habitat train split (in 3 languages) + ~1M marky-mT5 synthetic instruction-trajectory pairs for pretraining; the waypoint predictor uses the graph dataset of Hong et al. 2022
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D, with multiple views obtained by rotating the agent
setting.action_space: predicted waypoints as subgoals, executed as low-level forward 0.25 m / turn actions with tryout escape actions
setting.simulator: Habitat (Matterport3D scenes), no-sliding setting for evaluation

numbers.backbone: HAMT-based planner + CWP + tryout (model#2: with mT5 pretraining, no style transfer or ensemble)
numbers.extra: RxR-Habitat 2022 leaderboard submission; no-sliding; marky-mT5 pretraining
marky-mT5 pretraining, style-transfer augmentation, snapshot ensemble of two checkpoints; English val-unseen

numbers_note: The leaderboard submission used model#2 rather than the full model#4 because of the submission time limit. In the text the model#1 ablation is described as '41.65% SR', but Table 1 lists 47.56 SR and 41.65 SPL.
results: Reborn won the RxR-Habitat 2022 competition on test-unseen with NDTW 55.43 and SR 45.82, versus the best baseline CWP-RecBert (NDTW 37.30, SR 24.85) and CWP-CMA (NDTW 37.39). This is roughly a 48% relative NDTW gain and a 90% SR gain. The full model reaches 64.64 NDTW / 49.6 SR on English val-unseen.
limitations: The final leaderboard entry did not include style transfer or the snapshot ensemble, because of the submission deadline.
The tryout controller is a heuristic, and a gap to the sliding-allowed upper bound remains (48.6 vs 51.98 SR); overall performance is still far from perfect.
The waypoint predictor needs extra in-place rotation views, which consume action steps.
builds_on: CWP (Bridging the gap, Hong et al. 2022)
